page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-192GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, with 16 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the poor and weak categories respectively. However, multi-core performance is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all registering in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also perform at an average level, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high memory density, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory capacity but do not demand continuous, high-performance single-core CPU execution. It is well-suited for memory-intensive operations such as database caching, medium-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It is less suitable for single-threaded applications or heavy LLM text generation due to its weaker single-core and text generation benchmarks.
